newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes close down on demand, volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes close down on demand, volatile trade.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed 50 basis points down at 22 percent after seesawing at light trade, traders said.
The same-day rate varied between 19 percent and 23.25 percent during the session.
"Government rates were somewhat volatile. Demand for paper by those who had yet to cover positions tended to push rates down," said a trader.
"Nonetheless, many trades were small, 19 percent were for less than one million (pesos)," he added.
Some traders said overnight rates fell because Banco de Mexico bought paper to cover a higher liquidity injection than usual.

"People began to trade on rumors that Banco de Mexico withdrew large amounts of paper and they bought at low rates as they needed to cover positions. Overnight rates will be back at 22 percent to 23 percent on Monday though," another trader said. Liquidity shortages on Friday were exacerbated by 7.5 billion pesos in corporate tax payments, traders said. Banco de Mexico injected 8.321 billion pesos in liquidity by auctioning five credits.
Overnight rates on bank paper, meanwhile, closed 20 basis points down at 24.30 percent.
Credit maturities for Monday were estimated at 5.845 billion pesos, which was expected to put pressure on liquidity.
